alerts.title: Uncontrolled hypothyroidism despite levothyroxine
alerts.message: Patient has TSH 12.4 mIU/L (target below 4.5) with low Free T4, dry skin, periorbital puffiness, delayed ankle reflexes, constipation, tiredness, and cold intolerance — all consistent with inadequately treated hypothyroidism. She reports often forgetting the thyroid tablet, which is the likely primary cause. The clinician's plan to continue levothyroxine 50 mcg without dose adjustment or adherence counselling does not address this. Uncontrolled hypothyroidism can also contribute to weight gain, hyperlipidemia, and low mood, confounding attribution of these issues to DTG.

evidence.recommended_action: Address levothyroxine adherence with counselling, repeat TSH after consistent dosing, and consider dose increase if TSH remains elevated despite improved adherence.

alerts.title: Weight gain: DTG vs hypothyroidism attribution
alerts.message: Patient gained 9 kg in one year (72→84 kg, BMI 33) on TLD since January 2023. DTG is associated with weight gain, but uncontrolled hypothyroidism (TSH 12.4, low Free T4) is a significant alternative or contributing cause. The clinician plans to switch from DTG due to weight gain, but has not first corrected the hypothyroidism. Switching DTG before optimizing thyroid management risks unnecessary ART change without addressing a treatable cause. The dyslipidemia (LDL 4.2, total cholesterol 6.4) may also be partly hypothyroidism-related.

evidence.recommended_action: Optimize hypothyroidism treatment and reassess weight before switching DTG. If weight persists after euthyroid, then consider DTG substitution per guidelines.

alerts.title: DTG hyperglycemia risk: BMI ≥25 requires glucose monitoring
alerts.message: Guidelines state that patients on DTG with 2 or more risk factors for hyperglycemia (age ≥30, BMI ≥25, family history of DM, history of hypertension) should have glucose checked, with RBS every 3 months in the first 12 months for high-risk patients. This patient has age ≥30 and BMI 33 (≥25), meeting 2 risk factors. Fasting glucose 5.6 is currently normal, but ongoing monitoring is indicated. The clinician's plan does not include glucose monitoring.

evidence.recommended_action: Perform RBS every 3 months for first 12 months given BMI ≥25 and age ≥30, then use clinical indications to determine testing frequency.

alerts.title: TDF renal monitoring overdue by >12 months
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR every 12 months for experienced patients on TDF. The last creatinine was 196 days before the visit (2025-08-12), but no creatinine was ordered today. While the previous value (72 umol/L) was normal, the 12-month monitoring interval is approaching and no renal monitoring is in the clinician's plan. TDF nephrotoxicity can develop insidiously.

evidence.recommended_action: Order serum creatinine and eGFR now and ensure annual renal monitoring continues for as long as patient remains on TDF.
